task_name: A live session carries the program it runs

rubric.result: The objective promises that `PtyLiveSessions.open` spawns whatever program it is handed instead of always the login shell. Both halves are in the diff: `open(program: SessionProgram)` now spawns `program.file` with `[...program.argv]`, `cwd: program.cwd` and `env: PtyLiveSessions.#withForcedTerm(program.env)` (backend/src/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.ts:60-68), and the login shell it used to hardcode is now built by the new static `loginShell` and handed in by the entrypoint (ct-api.ts:421). Nothing about the shell is decided inside `open` any more: the session name comes from `program.name` and so do both stderr announcements. The 'so a conversation can be opened beside it' clause is served by the same signature and needs no further line in this task.

The `**TDD:**` line asks for `it('spawns the program it is given, with its own argv and working directory')` with the spawn double recording `file`, `argv` and `cwd` and the assertion on the literal three, with a program that is not a shell. The test at pty-live-sessions.test.ts:278-291 builds `new SessionProgram({ name: 'coordinator', file: '/usr/local/bin/claude', argv: ['--resume', 'abc123'], cwd: '/repo/governed-checkout', env: { PATH: '/usr/bin' } })` and asserts exactly `calls[0].file === '/usr/local/bin/claude'`, `calls[0].argv` equal to `['--resume', 'abc123']` and `calls[0].options.cwd === '/repo/governed-checkout'` — same assertion, same input, same expected values, and `claude` is not a shell. The second one the line asks for, `it('forces its own TERM over the program environment')` (line 293), feeds a program whose env carries `TERM: 'dumb'` and asserts the spawned env is strictly `{ PATH: '/usr/bin', TERM: PtyLiveSessions.TERM }`, which is the limit that sentence fixes.

Checked symbol by symbol against the brief's three blocks. `SessionProgram` (backend/src/domain/value-objects/session-program.ts) declares `name`, `file`, `argv: readonly string[]`, `cwd`, `env: Readonly<Record<string, string>>` and the constructor parameter object typed `name: unknown, file: unknown, argv: readonly string[], cwd: unknown, env: Readonly<Record<string, string>>` — the brief's Contract block literally. `open(program: SessionProgram): LiveSession` spawns `program.file` with `program.argv`, `cwd: program.cwd`, forces `TERM` over `program.env` and names the session `program.name`, as the brief states. `loginShell(shell: string | undefined, cwd: string, env)` is the new static and builds the `SessionProgram` with `FALLBACK_SHELL` as the fallback, `LOGIN_INTERACTIVE` as the only argv entry and `#basenameOf(file)` as the name. `ct-api.ts:421` reads `liveSessions.open(PtyLiveSessions.loginShell(environment.SHELL, process.cwd(), environment))`, the single occurrence the third verification command counted. The `shell`, `cwd` and `env` constructor fields are gone from the adapter together with their only reader, and no caller anywhere in `backend/` still passes them (grep over `new PtyLiveSessions(` finds ct-api.ts and the three test files, all on the three-field constructor). The guard messages quote what they got, as `live-session.ts` does.

Row by row: D-10 ('everything new under backend/ is TypeScript') — the new module is `session-program.ts` and uses only erasable syntax, so it complies. D-16 ('no new module under backend/src names cmux, no new test requires it') — `session-program.ts` names nothing of the sort and no test added here touches cmux. D-1 (the entrance is a real terminal in a PTY) — the diff serves it by letting that PTY carry a program other than the shell, and contradicts nothing in it. D-11, D-13, D-18, D-21, D-22, D-25, D-26 and the button literal row all bear on endpoints, phases, gates or frontend copy that this task does not touch; the diff leaves every one of them alone. No row is implemented with a value other than the one stated.

Exemplar: `backend/src/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.ts` is the named PTY adapter and the diff plays its own role in it — statics for the constants, private statics for the helpers, the port's other methods untouched; the new value object copies `backend/src/domain/value-objects/live-session.ts` idiom exactly (typed `unknown` in, non-empty-string guard quoting what it got with `JSON.stringify`, assignment, `Object.freeze(this)`). Rules opened and applied: `conventions/style.md` — no comment or docstring anywhere in the diff, every identifier and test name in English, and every function hangs off a type (`SessionProgram`, `PtyLiveSessions`, and in the test `Cabin`, `LoginProgram`, `OpenedTerminal`, `SpawnDouble`); `conventions/architecture.md` — the layers hold, `session-program.ts` imports nothing and infrastructure imports it downward, and `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`'s layout rule ('domain/value-objects, domain/ports and domain/policies are the three kinds of domain inhabitant apart from each other') is what puts the file where the brief's `**Files:**` puts it; `conventions/boundaries.md` — `loginShell` is the one door where `NodeJS.ProcessEnv` enters, `#definedEntriesOf` drops the undefined entries there and the type `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` keeps them out downstream, with no cast; `conventions/simplicity.md` — every new field and the new public static have a caller today (`ct-api.ts:421` and the adapter itself), and the guard sits at the door with no second opinion below it; `conventions/decisions.md` — 'TERM is forced' is decided once, in `#withForcedTerm`, and the fallback shell once, in `loginShell`; `conventions/domain.md` — `SessionProgram` names what the domain needs (a program, its argv, its cwd, its env) and no tool: swapping node-pty for another spawner leaves the name true. Delivery shape: no document of either yardstick prescribes expand-contract here, and in any case the signature change leaves no caller on the old path — typecheck is green and the grep finds no `open()` without a program. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no value that classifies anything is introduced, no dispatch and no catch-all; `name` is a label rendered in the session and in the stderr line, never compared to decide; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — the only maps are the process environment, which is a map by the OS's own contract; `#definedEntriesOf` feeds it into the value object at the door and `#withForcedTerm` is the one last step before the `spawn` call, and no module receives it and decides anything with it; (3) two fields that have to agree — `name` and `file` carry no agreement invariant (the new test names a program `coordinator` over the file `claude`), `file` is always a non-empty string with no sentinel, and the `shell: string | undefined` parameter is an absence resolved at the door into `FALLBACK_SHELL`, never stored as a sentinel; (4) an error named for where it happens — the two guards throw with messages that say what happened ("a session program's name must be a non-empty string, got …"), naming no module, and no new error type or family is introduced. The skills §3 names were loaded: `backend-engineering:backend-best-practices` is a Python router that `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` ranks third and explicitly makes yield, and nothing in it bears on this diff beyond the frozen value object and doubled port it already satisfies; `frontend-engineering:frontend-best-practices` has no subject, the diff touching no frontend file. Two observations that stay out of the findings because they are the plan's calls and not the implementer's: the brief's Contract block is what places `SessionProgram` in its own module while today its only production consumer is `pty-live-sessions.ts`, and the brief's `**Tests:**` is what asks for `names the login shell by its basename` beside the pre-existing `opening names the session after the program it runs`, which already covers the basename.

The `-` lines in the three test files are all the same rewiring: the `shell`, `cwd` and `env` overrides of `Cabin.opening` and `OpenedTerminal.with` disappear and each test now hands `open` a program built with the very same values (`PtyLiveSessions.loginShell('/usr/local/bin/fish', Cabin.CWD, { PATH: '/usr/bin' })`, and `process.env.SHELL, process.cwd(), process.env` in the two real-process files). Not one assertion is removed, relaxed or rewritten: `the shell is the login interactive one, and /bin/sh when SHELL is unset` keeps its full `toStrictEqual` over file, argv and the five options; `the environment carries TERM and no undefined entry` keeps both assertions and still reaches the undefined-dropping code, which moved from `open` to `loginShell` and sits on the path the test drives; both stderr tests keep their literal expected lines. The brief asks for exactly this: 'Existing tests keep their names, rebuilt around `loginShell`'.

The promised behaviour lives in production code: `open` reads `program.file`, `program.argv`, `program.cwd` and `program.env` at backend/src/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.ts:60-68, and `loginShell` at lines 48-58 is what still produces the shell's own program. The test's scaffolding (`SpawnDouble`, `TerminalDouble`, `Cabin`, `LoginProgram`, `OpenedTerminal`) only doubles the external system — the node-pty spawn — and records what it was handed; no expected value is hard-coded on the production side and no behaviour is simulated in the double. Reverting the production hunks would make all three new tests fail (and stop typechecking), so none of them passes on scaffolding alone.

Read inside the declared files. `session-program.ts` holds the value object and nothing else. `pty-live-sessions.ts` changes only what the Contract block asks for: the constructor loses three fields, `open` gains its parameter, `loginShell` is added, and `#environmentOf` splits into `#withForcedTerm` (the 'forcing TERM over program.env' sentence) and `#definedEntriesOf` (the filtering that had to move to the door where `NodeJS.ProcessEnv` still arrives) — both halves are required by the new signature, neither is an opportunistic refactor. `ct-api.ts` changes two lines, the construction and the call. The test files change only the plumbing the new signature forces plus the three tests `**Tests:**` names. Nothing under `### Out of scope` is touched: no brainstorming skill, no `/start-plan` use case, no gate, no `Home` stage. There is no hunk of the plan file in this diff, so there is no amendment to rule on.

Three new tests, at pty-live-sessions.test.ts:278, 293 and 306. Deterministic: no clock, no network, no randomness — ids come from `Ids.sequential()`, the paths are strings never touched on disk, and nothing sleeps. Isolated: `OpenedTerminal.with` builds a fresh `SpawnDouble.recording()` and a fresh `PtyLiveSessions` per test, mutating no shared state and depending on no order. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the doubled external system was handed (`spawn.calls[0].file`, `.argv`, `.options.cwd`, `.options.env`), which is the literal request `conventions/testing.md` prescribes for an adapter, and on the `name` that `loginShell` computed — all of which stop being true if the production hunks are reverted. Beyond the three: I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and found nothing in it or its `testing-anti-patterns.md` companion that these tests contradict and that is the implementer's to answer — its 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' would bite the name `spawns the program it is given, with its own argv and working directory`, but that name and that three-part assertion are written literally in the task's `**TDD:**` line, so the text the implementer was given and the skill cannot both be satisfied and the defect, if it is one, is the plan's.
